headline: Every species evolved in a place—adapted to specific conditions that shaped everything about it
universal_truth: Context shapes identity; where you develop determines what you become
fun_facts: Island species often evolve to be larger or smaller than their mainland relatives—the 'island rule'
Australia's unique mammals evolved in isolation for 45 million years
Invasive species cause billions of dollars in damage when introduced to ecosystems they didn't evolve in
discussion_questions: Why can't all species survive everywhere?
What happens when species are moved to places they didn't evolve?
How does your environment shape who you are?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Polar bears can't survive in jungles. Tropical fish die in cold water. Every species evolved in a particular place—adapted to specific temperatures, predators, food sources, and conditions. Move them, and they often fail. Place matters.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Species seem to 'fit' their environments perfectly. But this isn't design—it's the result of evolution in place. How does location shape what species become?

options.text: Natural selection in each location favors traits that work there—over millions of years, species become specialized
options.response: Yes. Evolution is local. The pressures of each environment select for different traits. What survives in one place might fail in another.

options.text: Species choose to live where they're best adapted
options.response: Species can't choose—they're shaped by where they happen to evolve...

q1.title: Local Adaptation
q1.script: Each environment presents unique challenges: cold, heat, drought, predators, competition. Over generations, populations adapt to local conditions. A species in the desert differs from its relatives in the rainforest—shaped by where it lives.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Local Adaptation"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Island Evolution
q2.script: Islands are evolution laboratories. Isolated populations evolve independently. Australia's mammals are unlike any others—45 million years of separate evolution. The Galápagos finches helped Darwin discover evolution itself.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Invasive Disasters
q3.script: When species move to new places—often by human transport—they can devastate local ecosystems. Without their native predators or diseases, invasive species multiply unchecked. Rabbits in Australia, kudzu in America: ecological catastrophes.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Context shapes identity. Species teach that where you develop determines what you become. This applies beyond biology—your environment shapes you too.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 152—welcome to June's Innovation month! Tomorrow, we'll discover why animals travel. Until then, consider how your environment has shaped who you are.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Environment Reflection - Where Shaped You?
growTrack.learning_objective: Recognize how environment shaped your identity
growTrack.activity: Consider how your environment shaped you—your hometown, family, culture, era. What would be different if you'd grown up somewhere else? Like species, you've been adapted by your context. What traits came from where you developed?
